findings.detail: Commit or stage a gitlink update that changes module/file, leaving the child checkout clean. The parent bucket contains module, while the child scope has no changed files because collection uses --base HEAD. The rendered --submodule=diff command shows module/file, but editing that reviewed file makes changes report it in outside_scope. Expand precise child-file membership for gitlink transitions so legitimate edits to reviewed content are recognized without authorizing unrelated child files.
findings.evidence: Both collectors invoke child collection with --base HEAD at review-scope:328 and extend only child staged, unstaged and untracked buckets at lines 355-359. The committed fixture explicitly asserts committed == ["module"]. Installed Git documentation confirms --submodule=diff displays internal content differences. codex-aspects subtracts exact bucket paths at lines 1157-1166 and grants directory coverage only for untracked repositories, leaving module/file outside scope.
findings.title: Parallel paths: gitlink diffs expose child files absent from editable scope

findings.detail: An untracked symlink such as module/new-link now enters the captured parent scope through recursive collection, but the prescribed symlink-discovery command still enumerates only the parent repository. It misses that link. When intent-to-add preparation is declined and the reviewer reads untracked paths directly, the link can be supplied without its required link-only annotation, exposing target contents. Inspect captured recursive paths rather than rediscovering only parent untracked files.
findings.evidence: Both collectors prefix child untracked paths at review-scope:355-359. reviewers.md:178-182 instead scans one parent-level review_git ls-files --others invocation. The shared wrapper adds only diff.ignoreSubmodules configuration. Installed git-ls-files documentation specifies explicit recursion and supports it only for cached/stage modes. The sibling codex-aspects renderer correctly checks each flattened untracked path with -L.
findings.title: Parallel paths: symlink discovery omits recursive untracked paths

findings.detail: This explanation predates the change. It attributes correct disk-tree hashing to seeding the temporary index from HEAD instead of the caller's index. The implementation deliberately copies the caller's index and uses --renormalize to avoid trusting its stat cache. The test remains useful, but its explanation names the opposite strategy.
findings.evidence: tests/scrut/review-scope.md:531-532 says seeding from HEAD keeps the trees equal. working_tree_digest copies real_index into tmp_index and then performs add --all --renormalize. scope-and-snapshot.md explains both requirements correctly. The same inaccurate sentence exists at the supplied merge base.
findings.title: Docs drift: digest test explanation describes the opposite index strategy
